html:
The Duchy of Swabia was one of the five great stem duchies of the medieval German kingdom, in the southwest around Lake Constance and the upper Rhine and Danube. It is on the map for 1000.

It arose in the 900s in the land settled by the Alemanni in late Roman times, inside East Francia. Its territory reached from Alsace to the Lech and south into today's Switzerland. The German kings often gave it to their own relatives to keep it loyal.

From 1079 the dukes came from the Hohenstaufen family, who later became kings and emperors of the Holy Roman Empire, among them Frederick II. When the last of them, Conradin, was beheaded in Naples in 1268, the duchy broke into many small lordships and free cities. The name lives on in the region of Swabia.
